title: Perfection and imperfection of saints' works
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Daily remission stands as needed; no one first gave toward God so as toward be repaid. Condign and congruent merit stand as toward be rejected; God crowns His own gifts in us, not our merits. — VII–VIII. On perfection: we assert that ye saints' good works in this life stand as not perfect by ye law's measure. That imperfection appears often as toward parts, always as toward degrees.
pass_b_english: VII–VIII. On perfection: we assert that the saints' good works in this life are not perfect by the law's measure. That imperfection appears often as to parts, always as to degrees.
Daily remission is needed; no one first gave to God so as to be repaid. Condign and congruent merit are to be rejected; God crowns His own gifts in us, not our merits.
source_text: VII. De perfectione: asserimus bona sanctorum opera in hac vita non esse perfecta ad mensuram legis. VIII. Ea imperfectio frequentissime ratione partium, semper vero ratione graduum. Opus est quotidiana remissione; nemo prior dedit Deo ut retribuatur ei. Meritum condignum et congruum repudiandum; Deus coronat in nobis sua dona, non nostra merita (Augustine).
